chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The origins of disbelief are three: greed, arrogance, and envy. As for greed, when Adam (peace be upon him) was forbidden from the tree, greed carried him to eat from it; and as for arrogance, it was Iblees when he was commanded to prostrate to Adam, so he refused; and as for envy, it was the two sons of Adam when one of them killed his companion.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three root causes of disbelief according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies three root causes of disbelief (kufr): greed (al-hirs), arrogance (al-istikbar), and envy (al-hasad). He illustrates each with a primordial example from the Quranic narrative: Adam's eating from the forbidden tree due to greed, Iblees's refusal to prostrate due to arrogance, and Qabil's murder of Habil due to envy. This triad is significant in Shia scholarship as it links the metaphysical origins of kufr to human psychological traits, providing a framework for spiritual self-purification (tazkiyah).
